questions_and_answers.question: Which grammatical dimensions are the focus of this unit?
In Hindi, the pronoun 'आप' always requires which type of verb?
According to the explanation, when is the plural form used for a single person?
What are the first person pronouns introduced in this unit?
Which singular third person pronoun means 'this one' and can be translated as he, she, or it?
What plural pronouns correspond to 'यह' and 'वह'?
How do you clearly indicate a group of people when using plural pronouns?

answers.answer: Add the noun 'लोग' after the pronoun

articles.text:
These पाठ are mainly concerned with three grammatical dimensions which go under the traditional names of gender, number and person.

Gender:

The two genders, 'masculine' and 'feminine', were introduced in पाठ 6 as far as nouns are concerned. Marked adjectives adjust their endings according to the noun they refer to. (पाठ 12-14) Expressions which refer to people also have gender, according to the sex of the person. (पाठ 10) (का phrases are like adjectives.)

Number:

Number is a two-way distinction: singular vs. plural. Hindi is much like English in its use of number. The pronoun आप for instance, always requires the plural verb हैं , just as English you requires the plural are. It can mean one person or several--no matter. आप is grammatically plural, always.

The plural number is used in referring to a group of persons or things; in referring to one person, the plural shows respect. Only children or persons of low rank should be talked about in the singular.

Person; the personal pronouns

It is customary to refer to three grammatical persons. The first person pronouns are मैं and हम. They require the verbs हूँ and हैं , respectively. आप is the only second person pronoun taught in this Introduction.

The singular third person pronouns are यह and वह. यह means this one, and is often translated he, she, or it. वह means that person or that thing, as well as he, she, it. The plurals are ये and वे. They can be translated they, these, or those. When they refer to a single person, they are translated he or she. (In informal speech, many people say ये for both यह and ये, and वो for both वह and वे.)

यह, ये, वह, and वे or any noun can be substituted in the third person examples.

All of the grammatically plural pronouns can refer to one person (Many people use हम to mean I.) To make it clear that a group of people is meant, the noun लोग is often added:

आप लोग — you-all
वे लोग — those people, they
हम लोग — we (not only I)

The following examples show how person, number, and gender combine in a sentence consisting of a pronoun or noun as subject, a marked adjective, and a verb.

1 s f    मैं थकी हूँ ।      I'm tired. (woman speaking)
1 s m    मैं भूखा हूँ ।      I'm hungry. (man speaking)
2 p f    आप अच्छी हैं ।      You're O.K. (to a woman)
2 p m    आप गोरे हैं ।       You're fair. (to a man)
1 p m    हम बूढ़े हैं ।       We are old. I am old.
3 s f    नदी गहरी है ।       The river is deep.
3 s m    पानी गंदा है ।       The water is dirty.
3 p f    सड़कें चौड़ी हैं ।    The streets are wide.
3 p m    वे काले हैं ।       They are black.

(The other possibility, first person plural feminine, is rare.)

The present participle consists of the root of the verb plus one of the endings ता ते ती. Here is the full list for the verb go:

Person   Gender  Number
मैं जाता हूँ    1   mas. sing.
मैं जाती हूँ    1   fem. sing.
हम जाते हैं    1   mas. pl.
आप जाते हैं    2   mas. pl.
आप जाती हैं    2   fem. pl.
यह जाता है    3   mas. sing.
ये जाते हैं    3   mas. pl.
यह जाती है    3   fem. sing.
ये जाती हैं    3   fem. pl.

Another form is the root plus the ending ना ; this is called the infinitive. This is the form listed in the dictionary. The verbs introduced on page 36 (in their infinitive form):

बोलना    speak
खाना     eat
सीखना    learn
पढ़ाना    teach
जानना    know
लिखना    write
पढ़ना    study, read
पकाना    prepare
समझना    understand
पहनना    wear, put on
खेलना    play
पीना     drink
